parts.note: a tiny web-spinning creature thought to bring good fortune, which also literally hangs (depends) from its thread

explanation.surface: A gadget-like spinning toy might be handy, but whether it is depends on circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It depends' reads as a shrug, but 'depend' also means hang down, as a small spider does from its silk; superstition says this tiny spider brings wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore holds that this tiny spider brings riches to whoever it lands on, and it dangles from a thread.

clue.text: French dramatist has to rest longer outside

indicators.note: outside tells us the word for longer wraps around the word for rest

parts.note: longer means more (as in 'no more' time)
to rest is to lie down

explanation.surface: A French playwright needs a longer nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the great seventeenth-century French comic playwright.

clue.text: Name house put up in Southern France

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word for house is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house

explanation.surface: Someone names a house they have built in the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' looks like building, but it reverses the semi; 'in' is a link, the definition being a place found in Southern France. A SEMI is the British term for a semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: Nîmes is a Roman city in the Gard department of southern France.

indicators.note: letters given treatment are worked over and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An undersized child is taken to the doctor for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for treatment' makes the anagram of RUNTY plus GOES.
explanation.definitionFit: A kid is a child, a young person.

definitions.meaning: a single leaf of a book or paper
Buttons is a traditional nickname for a hotel pageboy, from the rows of buttons on his uniform

explanation.surface: A sheet made of buttons, perhaps a sewing pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buttons' is British slang for a uniformed hotel boy, and the name of that character in pantomime Cinderella; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf of a book is called this, and so is a young uniformed attendant nicknamed Buttons.

parts.note: the sleepy guest at the Mad Hatter's tea party in Alice in Wonderland, stuffed into the teapot

explanation.surface: A politician from some party whose career fell apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went to pot' sounds like ruin, but in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland the Hatter and March Hare push a sleepy creature into the teapot.
explanation.definitionFit: The drowsy rodent at the Mad Hatter's tea party ends up being put into the teapot.

clue.text: A northern line first to show mountain-ash

indicators.note: first places the word for line ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A northern rail line must first display a mountain tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to show' is a link. 'Northern line' looks like the London Tube line, but the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: This tree with red berries is commonly called the mountain ash.

clue.text: Fragrant water from mountain-pass, gone for processing

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountain peaks

indicators.note: something sent for processing is worked over, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Perfumed water from a mountain pass has been sent off to be processed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for processing' makes the anagram OGNE of GONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de Cologne is a light scented water, named after the German city.

parts.note: the saying 'he who waits and dithers is lost' tells you which action makes you lost

explanation.surface: Someone becomes absorbed in an old saying.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'He who hesitates is lost', so the action that causes you to get lost in it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver or pause before acting is what the proverb says leads to being lost.

clue.text: Miler in trouble round town-hard cheese!

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters go around the word for town
letters in trouble are disturbed and jumbled into a new order

parts.note: a burg is a town

explanation.surface: A runner in difficulty around town is having bad luck: hard cheese!
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' makes LIMER from MILER, and 'round' puts it around BURG. 'Hard cheese' is also a British exclamation meaning bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Limburger is a strong-smelling cheese from the Limburg region of Belgium and the Netherlands.

clue.text: Circle in which cad chases women

indicators.note: chases means the cad's word comes after the letter for women

parts.note: a heel is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A scoundrel runs after women in some social circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel is a round shape, a ring.

clue.text: England's openers receive warning and flag

parts.note: the opening two letters of England
a sign can be a warning, an omen

explanation.surface: England's opening batsmen get a warning and a flag is raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receive' and 'and' are links. Openers are cricket's first two batsmen, so England's openers are its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag, especially one flown by a ship to show nationality.
Indicating something is doing this; repairing mortar joints in a wall is also called this.

clue.text: Exhausted English very loud, taking summer in France

parts.note: ff (fortissimo) is the musical marking for very loud
été is French for summer

explanation.surface: An English person, worn out and noisy, takes a summer holiday in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means feeble and worn out, having lost vigour.

parts.note: lawless means uncontrolled, unruly

explanation.surface: A man makes a wild, uncontrolled noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. 'sound' looks like a noun for noise, but it is the adjective meaning undamaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound in the sense of perfect and without defect.

indicators.note: changed means these letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A judge has rearranged when afternoon tea is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a quantity roughly is to gauge or calculate it approximately.

definitions.meaning: a grammatical tense for incomplete past action

explanation.surface: Is the grammar of this tense wrong?
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical tense ('was walking') bears this name, which also means flawed.

clue.text: Train Bill to take copper? Most unusual!

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of most arranged in an odd order

explanation.surface: A man called Bill arresting a policeman would be most unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' is a link; 'unusual' makes STOM from MOST. 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone in a habit is to get them used to it.

clue.text: Put on heavy music-it is symbolic of Ireland

parts.note: to put on is to feign, sham
heavy rock music

explanation.surface: Someone plays loud music as an emblem of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-leaved clover is the national emblem of Ireland, linked with St Patrick.

definitions.meaning: to fancy is to think something likely, to guess
a person the police detain on suspicion

explanation.surface: A lover is detained by police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy-man' is a lover, but the hyphen splits two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose something is true, and a person the police think may be guilty.

definitions.meaning: to mushroom is to grow and expand rapidly
in American usage, a ranch or farm

explanation.surface: Is there a mushroom farm in the United States?
explanation.definitionFit: To expand quickly, and an American word for a big ranch.

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, with the possessive s
sent means directed somewhere

explanation.surface: A girl has been told to refuse her consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To disagree with an official view, refusing agreement.

clue.text: Converted lira sum — O! It contains tanners

indicators.note: money converted changes form, so these letters change their order

explanation.surface: Someone changes a sum of lira and exclaims at what it contains: old sixpences!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanners' looks like British slang for old sixpence coins, fitting the currency surface, but it means sunbathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunroom where people sunbathe, or a room with sunbeds.

clue.text: Memento of priest in his church

indicators.note: in places the priest inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: RC is short for Roman Catholic church
Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A keepsake from a priest in his own church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'his' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object kept as a reminder of a person or past time.

definitions.meaning: graded music exams, such as the eight British levels

explanation.surface: Classes for music examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. In Britain, music exams are taken in numbered levels.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranks or levels, and the numbered stages of music examinations.
To go somewhere by car, and a strong inner motivation.

clue.text: She helped to raise the Siamese issue

definitions.text: She helped to raise the Siamese issue

parts.words: She helped to raise the Siamese issue
parts.note: the English governess who taught the King of Siam's children, as in The King and I

explanation.surface: A woman helped bring up some question about Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' seems to be a political question, but it means offspring: Anna Leonowens was governess to the children of King Mongkut of Siam.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Leonowens was governess to the children of the Siamese king.

parts.note: ease means comfort

explanation.surface: Someone abandons comfort for their patronage of the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. 'Art supporter' looks like a patron.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's stand holds the canvas up.

parts.note: a small citrus fruit with easily peeled skin, not a Chinese official in a robe

explanation.surface: A Chinese official wearing a baggy coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mandarin' suggests an official, but it is the fruit, whose peel comes away easily.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loose-skinned orange is a variety of mandarin.

clue.text: Remark about role of non-smoker, for example

indicators.note: about means the word for remark goes around the word for role

parts.note: a comment is a remark
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: Someone comments on the role of a person who does not smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. A non-smoker was a railway carriage section where smoking was banned.
explanation.definitionFit: A section of a train carriage; a no-smoking one was an example.
